### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `04c80f1a8002a4786164316dfb6f5814db218bd2` — the merge of head `1c2b804052a59a3aa0d5b798da42ac3d81d80212` into base `5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 04c80f1a8002a4786164316dfb6f5814db218bd2 && git checkout 04c80f1a8002a4786164316dfb6f5814db218bd2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c 1c2b804052a59a3aa0d5b798da42ac3d81d80212 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c && git merge --no-ff 1c2b804052a59a3aa0d5b798da42ac3d81d80212

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-inert-object-declarations.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-semantic-roles.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.field-group-shadowed-six-highlights.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.publish-refuses-metadata-the-runtime-ignores.ts

Read: both cards with every comment, the PR body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...18224af0` (19 files, +197/−41, merge-base `e35cf035`), and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. The rest of the diff (the two test files, the three showcase objects, the generated `api-surface` / `export-origins` / `liveness` / `validation.mdx` output, the changesets) is the lane seat's ACCEPT and is not judged in ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`state-machine-no-initial-states` accepts a machine whose `events` leave out `insert` — right.** `runsOnInsert` returns true for an absent or `null` `events` and otherwise requires an array containing `insert`. That is the engine's own filter, `r.events ?? ['insert', 'update']` then `events.includes(mode)` (`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts:3938-3939`), and the only `initialStates` read sits under `if (mode === 'insert')` (`:4209-4210`). The schema default is `['insert', 'update']` (`validation.zod.ts:149`), and the rule is registered `input: 'parsed'` (`authoring-rules.ts`), so the predicate is right on a defaulted stack and on a raw one. The guard sits after the `active === false` skip and before the `initialStates` test, so a machine that runs on insert is refused exactly as before, with the same hint.
- **`events: []` is not judged — right for the server.** `[].includes('insert')` is false in the engine, so the machine never runs on create. See N3 for the client readers, which read an empty list differently.
- **A non-array `events` is not judged — right.** The schema refuses it before this rule's verdict can matter.
- **`field-group-shadowed` warns a group emptied by the fifth or sixth highlight — right.** The page cuts with the same constant in three places: `deriveHighlightFields` (`max = RECORD_HIGHLIGHTS_MAX`), `buildDefaultHighlights` and `headerDrawnFields`, and the last one is what the Details body leaves out.
- **No list warned under four passes under six — right.** The first-four set is a subset of the first-six set, so the hidden-from-body set only grows. The card's "a valid list is refused" half therefore does not occur, and the diff is right to add no carve-out. The card's own example agrees: `owner_id` in fourth position is hoisted on the page too.
- **New public export `RECORD_HIGHLIGHTS_MAX` on `@objectstack/spec/ui` — right, additive.** It reaches the barrel through `export * from './component.zod'`, and `api-surface/ui.json` and `export-origins/ui.json` carry the row. `@objectstack/lint` already imports values from `@objectstack/spec/ui` (`filter-walk.ts`, `i18n-walk.ts`), and the `ui/` packages already import values from it (`app-shell`), so neither import is a new dependency edge.
- **`plugin-detail` keeps its module export `RECORD_HIGHLIGHTS_MAX` as a re-export — right.** Same name, same value; the package entry (`src/index.tsx`) never exported it, and the in-package test still imports it from the module.
- **`validation.zod.ts` changes one `.describe()` string only — right.** No accept-set change; the regenerated `validation.mdx` carries the same sentence in its four places.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/35251-state-machine-update-only.md`: `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/spec` minor, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. Right: against `main` the rule accepts a declaration it refused, and a kind takes at least minor on each package the diff moves.
- `.changeset/35252-field-group-shadowed-six-highlights.md`: lint, spec and `@object-ui/plugin-detail` minor, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. Right: a requirement tightened (a new warning that `--strict` turns into exit 1). It carries the fix in the body and the one ADR-0087 marker, `registered field-group-shadowed-six-highlights`, and the entry file exists under that id.
- PR body: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the stronger of the two changesets on both lines. Right.
- Gate verdict: `Check Changeset` has two runs on this head. Run 44591918484 (the `synchronize` event) failed; its log ends on the declaration-line check and says the lines "are re-read from the body on the next `edited` event, so this clears with no push". Run 44592003459 (the `edited` event, started 30 seconds later) succeeded and is the newer run. The tree and the current body agree with the passing run. `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` and `Test UI` with all their shards, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Live E2E UI` and `Build Docs` all concluded success. Of the 74 runs, the only other non-success is one cancelled `PR-body guards` run with a later success beside it; the rest are skipped.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in both os-dev-reports (7018508222, 7019779056). Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, file surface widened to the spec describe, the regenerated mdx, the two upgrade-guide entries, the liveness note and the regenerated surface files: accepted. Each is prose the change made false or generated output a gate demands, and claim amendment 7018624230 records it.
- Deviation, two changesets where the fold claim said one: accepted. The two cards move the protocol in opposite directions, and one note could not state both arms.
- Deviation, `Metadata-protocol: added` on #35251 measured against `main` while the refusal it narrows is itself unreleased: accepted. The line follows the diff, and the changeset says the rule is the same release's.
- Deviation, the every-option `initialStates` residual (6992730706) untouched: accepted as out of scope. The diff does not change that verdict, and the claim sends it back to the seat to route.
- Deviation, the #35244 changeset sentence is now broader than the rule: accepted. Both notes are unreleased and ship together, and the #35251 note states the narrower rule.
- Out-of-scope finding, the stage field `headerDrawnFields` adds to the body-hidden set: filed as #35630. Confirmed by reading `headerDrawnFields`: the lint does not model `pathField`.
- Out-of-scope finding, `HIGHLIGHT_FIELDS_MAX` (Studio) and `HIGHLIGHTS_MAX` (`RecordHoverCard.tsx`): both read 6 on this head and neither decides a verdict. Noted, no card owed.
- Out-of-scope finding, the skills text: rides #35245, as the PR body's `Skills-docs:` line says.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts`** — holds. The new sentence says the rule refuses a machine "when its `events` include `insert` (the default)" and that an update-only machine "never runs on create, so it needs no `initialStates`". Both are true of the engine lines cited in ①, and the first consumer, `runsOnInsert`, implements exactly that sentence. The ruling it implements is the card's scope line, "the rule judges only machines that run on insert".

**`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`** — holds. Each jsdoc sentence was read against the synthesizer:
- "after the record's title field leaves the list, the DEFAULT record page draws in its header strip": `deriveHighlightFields` filters the title and then slices.
- "an entry past this count is drawn in the body instead": `headerDrawnFields` slices with the constant, so the seventh entry is not in the body-hidden set.
- "Not the bound of an authored `record:highlights` block's `fields`": `RecordHighlightsProps.fields` is `.max(7)`, a separate bound.
- A plain exported constant in this file has a precedent (`SECTION_HEADING_COUNT_HOLE`).
- The home is right: lint depends on spec and on nothing under `ui/`, so spec is the only package both readers can import.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-inert-object-declarations.ts`** — agrees with the contract. Tried to break it with `null`, `[]`, a non-array, a defaulted parse and a raw object; each lands where the engine does.

**`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`** and **`18.publish-refuses-metadata-the-runtime-ignores.ts`** — agree. Both now state the insert condition the rule applies.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-semantic-roles.ts`** — the cut and the hint agree with the constant and with the page's count. One sentence overstates; see N1.

**`ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts`** — agrees. Import plus re-export; no behaviour change.

**`18.field-group-shadowed-six-highlights.ts`** — agrees: a warning, not a publish refusal, a group warned before is still warned, and `--strict` exits 1.

Nits, none of which changes a verdict of this diff:

- N1 (nit) — the lint's title ladder is not the renderer's, so the new comment in `validate-semantic-roles.ts`, "the verdict and the screen cannot drift apart", holds for the count only.
  - The lint reads `nameField`, then `displayNameField` (each only when it names a field), then the first of `name`, `full_name`, `title`, `subject`, `display_name` present by name.
  - The page reads `resolveNameField` (`ui/packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts`): the declared pointer, then a type-aware derivation that also takes `label`, the `*_name` / `*_title` / `name_*` affixes and, failing those, the first title-eligible field.
  - Where the two differ and the page's title is itself listed in `highlightFields`, the cut lands one entry apart. Example: an object with `account_name` and no `name`, seven highlights with `account_name` among the first six. The page hoists the seventh; the lint does not judge it.
  - The ladder lines are unchanged by this diff and the same gap existed under the four-cut, so this is not a regression. Read only, not reproduced on a running page.
  - Recommended: a follow-up card beside #35630 (or widen #35630) to have the lint take the title from the same resolver. A code-comment fix would move the head, so the sentence is left as an accepted deviation here.
